newsitem.title: USA: Packard Bell launches direct-sale strategy.
newsitem.headline: Packard Bell launches direct-sale strategy.

text.p: Packard Bell NEC Inc., the nation's second-largest personal computer supplier, said Wednesday it would start selling computer systems directly to small and medium-sized companies.

The direct-sales strategy, dubbed NEC NOW and scheduled for launch early in the third quarter, allows commercial users to combine the pricing advantages of direct sales with service and support from retail outlets if they want, the Sacramento, Calif.-based company said.

The success of Dell Computer Corp.'s model of selling PCs directly has led many companies to look at their current way of selling PCs, from Compaq Computer Corp. to Hewlett-Packard Co. -- and now Packard Bell NEC.

Packard Bell NEC's programme focuses on small and medium-size companies, the company said, adding it expected state, local and federal government agencies and educational institutions would also buy products via NEC NOW.
The company, the world's third-largest PC supplier after Compaq Computer Corp. and International Business Machines Inc., said it expected to double its sales force on the next few quarters.
The company is 20 percent owned by Japan's NEC Corp., 20 percent by France's Groupe Bull, with the rest held by private owners.
